article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 40% indica / 35% sativa / 25% ruderalis
Genetics: AK-47 × Ruderalis
Breeder: Royal Queen Seeds
THC Content: Up to approximately 15%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Earth, pepper, spice, sour herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 11–12 weeks total from germination
Outdoor Harvest Time: 75–85 days after sprouting
Indoor Yield: Up to 350 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 110–160 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

AK-47 became famous during an era when cannabis flavor was more likely to be described as spice, skunk, fruit, and hash than frosting or candy. AK-47 Auto carries some of that older personality into a plant designed around modern convenience. Royal Queen Seeds crossed AK-47 with ruderalis genetics to shorten the life cycle and remove the need for photoperiod control, producing compact marijuana that can move from sprout to harvest in roughly three months.

The finished flower does not chase extreme cannabinoid numbers; instead, its identity centers on a motivating, conversational effect and a savory combination of earth, pepper, sourness, and spice. For growers interested in classic genetics but unwilling or unable to manage a full photoperiod crop, this automatic version offers a practical route into one of weed breeding’s best-known families.
Genetics and Lineage

Royal Queen Seeds gives the direct formula as AK-47 × ruderalis. Behind the AK-47 side lies a more complicated international ancestry. Serious Seeds , breeder of the original AK-47, states that Simon developed the strain from Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock after extensive selection work in the early 1990s. Serious Seeds still keeps the precise recipe private, but confirms those four geographic sources and describes the original as a predominantly sativa hybrid.

RQS used AK-47 genetics as the foundation and introduced a high-performing ruderalis line to create automatic flowering. The resulting composition shifts to 40% indica, 35% sativa, and 25% ruderalis. That addition matters primarily in the garden: flowering begins according to plant maturity rather than requiring progressively longer nights. It also means Royal AK Auto is not genetically identical to the original Serious Seeds AK-47 or to AK-47 autoflowers sold by other breeders. The specifications in this profile refer specifically to Royal Queen Seeds’ version.
Effects and Experience

The experience is more cheerful than intimidating. Royal Queen Seeds characterizes the effects as motivating, giggly, and socially engaging, a notable contrast with the strain’s severe-sounding name. At moderate amounts, the mental shift can feel buoyant rather than foggy, with conversation flowing more naturally and routine activities gaining a little extra novelty. Creative hobbies, casual social settings, music, and daytime recreation fit the profile better than the heavy evening routine associated with strongly sedating indica weed.

With THC listed at up to 15%, potency is moderate by current high-THC standards, yet that does not make the flower non-intoxicating. Increasing the dose can turn a light cerebral buzz into a stronger change in perception, attention, and physical coordination. Individual tolerance also makes percentage comparisons imperfect. The CDC notes that cannabis can slow reaction time and decision-making, impair coordination, and distort perception, so even a strain described as motivating should never be used before driving or other safety-sensitive activities.
Medical Benefits

The moderate potency and upbeat character may interest some medical marijuana consumers who find very strong cannabis unnecessarily intense. A cultivar that combines mental lift with a comparatively manageable THC level might be considered by experienced patients seeking temporary changes in mood, appetite, stress, or physical comfort without deliberately pursuing deep sedation. However, AK-47 Auto itself has not been clinically established as a treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, fatigue, or another medical condition. A strain name is not a standardized pharmaceutical formulation.

RQS lists CBD only as “low,” which means the psychoactive experience remains primarily THC-driven. Although 15% THC is lower than many modern cultivars exceeding 20%, unwanted reactions are still possible. NIDA notes that cannabis can produce anxiety, fear, distrust, or panic in some people, particularly after larger amounts or exposure to stronger products. Anyone using weed alongside prescription medication or for persistent psychiatric, sleep, or pain-related symptoms should discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional and consider laboratory testing from the actual product being consumed.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Savory terpenes define Royal AK Auto more clearly than sweetness. During late flowering, RQS describes a pronounced scent of earth and pepper, and those aromas continue into the flavor alongside a noticeable sour accent. The overall impression can resemble dry soil, cracked pepper, herbs, and mild fermented sharpness rather than tropical fruit or dessert cream. That gives the flower a distinctly traditional cannabis character, especially compared with the heavily sweetened terpene profiles common in newer American hybrids.

Royal Queen Seeds does not publish a batch-specific terpene percentage chart for the automatic version. Its Royal AK photoperiod line, however, is described as carrying myrcene, caryophyllene, limonene, and pinene, with spice, skunk, and fresh lemon among the associated aromas. Those compounds provide useful family context but should not be treated as a guaranteed laboratory ratio for every Royal AK Auto harvest. The breeder-supported automatic profile remains primarily earthy, peppery, spicy, and sour.
Growing Information

Royal AK Auto was designed for uncomplicated cultivation. RQS recommends at least 18 hours of daily indoor light and reports plants reaching approximately 70–80 cm after the early flowering stretch, though outdoor specimens can grow closer to 100 cm. Indoor harvests reach about 350 g/m², while outdoor plants typically produce 110–160 g each. The complete growing period is approximately 11–12 weeks, with the breeder’s technical sheet listing 45–55 days for the flowering portion and 75–85 days after sprouting as a broader harvest reference.

Its compact dimensions make the plant suitable for smaller grow spaces, yet it can still develop enough branching to benefit from gentle canopy management. Royal Queen Seeds recommends low-stress training around the third week to reduce vertical stretch and improve light exposure across developing flower sites. Selective defoliation later can prevent leaves from shading productive growth. Because this is an autoflower, severe early stress is less forgiving than it would be with photoperiod cannabis; the plant continues toward flowering regardless of whether it has fully recovered.

Outdoor cultivation works on a calendar determined by germination rather than autumn daylight. That allows growers in suitable legal climates to finish plants before traditional photoperiod marijuana reaches maturity and potentially schedule more than one crop during a long season. RQS also notes that Royal AK Auto handles a variety of environments and performs well in somewhat cooler conditions. Strong early growth, adequate sunlight or indoor lighting, careful watering, and steady airflow remain more important than complicated training methods.
FAQ
Is AK-47 Auto indica or sativa?

Royal Queen Seeds classifies Royal AK Auto as 40% indica, 35% sativa, and 25% ruderalis. Although technically slightly indica dominant by percentage, its motivating, giggly, and social effects preserve much of the mentally lively personality associated with AK genetics.
What are the genetics of AK-47 Auto?

The RQS version is AK-47 × ruderalis. The original AK-47 parent developed by Serious Seeds traces to Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock, although breeder Simon has never publicly revealed the exact recipe or proportions of those landrace influences.
How strong is AK-47 Auto?

Royal Queen Seeds currently lists THC at up to 15% with low CBD. That places it below many contemporary 20–30% THC cultivars, but it can still produce significant intoxication, particularly for consumers with low tolerance.
How long does AK-47 Auto take to grow?
RQS gives a total life cycle of approximately 11–12 weeks, with its technical data listing harvest around 75–85 days after sprouting. Flowering itself generally occupies about 45–55 days.
How much does AK-47 Auto yield?

Indoor plants can produce up to approximately 350 g/m². Outdoor specimens generally yield around 110–160 g per plant under suitable conditions. Lighting, climate, root health, nutrition, and early plant development all influence final production.
Final Thoughts on AK-47 Auto

AK-47 Auto translates a historic cannabis family into a smaller, faster, and easier cultivation format without trying to compete in the modern race for maximum THC. Royal Queen Seeds combines AK-47 with ruderalis to create a compact automatic hybrid that reaches approximately 15% THC and finishes in about 11–12 weeks. The flavor stays rooted in earth, pepper, spice, and sourness, while the high favors laughter, motivation, and sociability over immediate couch-lock.

Its heritage adds another dimension. The AK side ultimately reaches back to Colombian, Mexican, Thai, and Afghan seed stock used by Serious Seeds to create the original AK-47 in 1992, connecting this modern automatic weed to one of the defining hybrid families of the 1990s. For growers, manageable size, straightforward training, respectable yields, and automatic flowering make it accessible without being uninteresting. For consumers, moderate potency and savory old-school flavor provide an alternative to today’s ultra-strong dessert hybrids. Keeping Royal Queen Seeds attached to the name remains important because other breeders produce different AK-47 autos, but within the RQS catalog, Royal AK Auto is a practical interpretation of a genuine cannabis classic.
